summary: SMPL FY25 10-K (filed 2025-10-28, FYE Aug 30 2025) framed Atkins as a managed transition, OWYN as an accretive acquisition, and Quest as a +11% growth engine. The two subsequent fiscal 2026 10-Qs (Q1 filed 2026-01-08, Q2 filed 2026-04-09) materially contradict all three: OWYN was impaired $187M (66% of the $282M June 2024 purchase price) just 20 months post-close after being declared NOT impaired qualitatively in the FY25 10-K; Atkins took a SECOND consecutive $62M impairment (on top of the FY25 $60.9M); and Quest growth has decelerated from +11.1% FY25 to +0.3% in Q2 FY26 (the company's only remaining growth engine stalled). Concurrently, the company executed $188M of debt-funded buybacks in H1 FY26 at an average $19.62 (cutoff price implied ~$13-14), the CEO was fired January 18 2026 and replaced by the prior CEO (Scalzo, 2017-2023), and a $15M restructuring is underway. Form 4 evidence is mixed: independent director James Kilts (former Gillette/Kraft CEO, Centerview founder) bought 80,000 shares for $991K on April 23 2026 (two weeks after the Q2 impairment), and director Clayton Daley Jr (former P&G CFO) bought 10,000 shares for $118K on May 14 2026 — meaningful informed-insider purchases into the drawdown. BUT the new interim CEO Joseph Scalzo SOLD $14.94M as a director in the year before being reappointed, and total 12-month insider sales ($24.7M) exceed purchases ($1.4M) at a 17:1 ratio. Verdict: SHORT-tier — three SEVERE underdeliveries (OWYN impairment, Atkins decay, Quest stall), one RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE (procyclical debt-funded buybacks), one SEVERE on CEO termination/restructuring. The Kilts/Daley purchases at $12 are notable but not large enough in dollar terms to offset $309.9M of cumulative intangible impairment, $188M of value-destroyed buybacks, and a strategy reset that requires the prior CEO to be recalled.
